public_rationale: The stated calculation holds: 55 million divided by the assumed 905 million is 6.08%. A larger monthly-user denominator would lower that share, as Zitron qualifies with “likely” and “in theory.” This supports the approximate, conditional estimate. It does not establish an exact monthly conversion rate or a measured rate of free users becoming paying customers.
limitations: The exact subscriber figure comes through secondary reporting because the original report was inaccessible.
Quarterly-average weekly users and subscriber counts are not fully aligned measurements.
The monthly-user evidence is contextual and partly extrapolated.

our_interpretation: The period is Q1 2026, identified in the surrounding discussion.
Conversion rate means the reported paying-subscriber count divided by the stipulated user base, rather than a measured rate of users purchasing subscriptions over time.
The monthly-user qualification expresses an expected denominator effect, not a claim to know an exact monthly conversion rate.
For comparable populations and nested observation windows, including less frequent users increases the denominator and lowers the paid share.
criteria.support_condition: The reported Q1 paying-subscriber count divided by the assumed 905 million users rounds to about 6%. The qualified monthly-user argument must be consistent with how broader activity windows affect the denominator.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable Q1 subscriber figures make the stipulated calculation materially different from 6%, or comparable activity measurements undermine the proposed denominator effect.
